name: Zayn al-Dīn Abū al-Ḥusayn Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbd al-Muʿṭī al-Zawāwī
summary: Maghribi grammarian who taught in Damascus and Cairo and wrote al-Durra al-alfiyya, the first thousand-verse grammar, which Ibn Mālik names at the start of his own Alfiyya.
bio: Ibn Muʿṭī came from the Berber Zawāwa of the central Maghrib, taught grammar in Damascus and then in Cairo, where he died in 628/1231.

His al-Durra al-alfiyya puts naḥw and ṣarf into a thousand verses; his al-Fuṣūl al-khamsūn sets them out in fifty short chapters. Ibn Mālik, a generation later, opens his own Alfiyya by saying it surpasses 'the Alfiyya of Ibn Muʿṭī', and then grants that Ibn Muʿṭī deserves praise for coming first. His poem was read and commented on until Ibn Mālik's took its place.
